body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\), only the inference branch additionally requires \(r<\min(n,m)\), the low-rank growth margin, deterministic polynomial-size dense average-scale loadings, variance nondegeneracy, and Belloni--Oliveira predictable-covariance stabilization. Under these conditions, the conditional leave-one-cell-out multiplier law consistently approximates \(\max_{g\in\mathcal G_n}|(\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g)/\widehat s_g|\). Thus \(P(\tau_g\in[\widehat\tau_g\pm c_{1-\alpha}\widehat s_g]\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G_n)\to1-\alpha\). Pointwise radii obey \(\widehat s_g=O_P(B/\sqrt{nmq})\), while \(c_{1-\alpha}=O_P(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|})\); this query-family multiplier is not part of \(b_{nm}\), and no rank restriction is added to Theorems 2--4.
body.justification: The result separates query multiplicity from row-factor recovery.
body.gap: Belloni and Oliveira's arXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 and Theorem 3.3 on page 8 give a generic martingale multiplier theorem after normalized increments and plug-in consistency are supplied. The lemma here derives those hypotheses for deterministic dense causal loadings and leave-one-cell-out low-rank residuals. Xia and Yuan's loading-alignment conditions are not used. Ma et al.'s published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 concern a coefficient matrix under modeled nonadaptive missingness.
body.consumer: HeartSteps II investigators can report familywise-valid proximal-effect averages.
